task: Fix PreviewLoader state so an older preview request cannot replace the newest selection during fetch or decode. Follow requirements.md, preserve the existing API and both existing tests unchanged, and retain rerunnable native regression tests. Cover initial/loading/ready/error states; overlap begun during each phase; identical keys as distinct requests; stale success and failure without overwriting a newer pending or settled state; per-instance isolation; exact key/bytes/signal/result/error identities; synchronous and asynchronous failures in both phases with recovery; and actual callback rejection on abort. Use the actual class and controlled callbacks, bound behavior-dependent waits, observe rejection promptly, settle owned callbacks and drain tasks on failure. Work only in this project; no dependencies, services, other skills, delegation, browser work or publishing.

files.requirements.md:
Runtime: installed Node.js, ES modules and node:test; run node --test. No dependencies or browser rendering.
PreviewLoader.state initially equals {status:'idle',value:null,error:null}. Each load invocation is a distinct request, even with identical keys. Before invoking fetchBytes, the newest call sets status to 'loading', preserves the currently displayed value and clears error. Only that instance's most recently invoked call may subsequently change state. Its success sets {status:'ready',value:<exact decoded result>,error:null}; its failure sets status:'error', preserves the displayed value and stores the exact rejection reason. A later invocation can recover.
Overlaps may begin while an earlier fetch or decode is pending. A stale request's success or failure must not replace any newer loading, ready or error state. This includes an older decode failure while the newest fetch remains pending. Different loader instances are independent.
All calls still run their own fetchBytes(key,signal) then decode(bytes,signal), including stale calls after successful fetch. Preserve those argument references, exact successful value and exact thrown/rejected reason. Fetch failure must not invoke decode. Synchronous callback throws become rejected load Promises, as in the existing async API. Do not suppress old callers' results or failures, deduplicate identical keys, or skip decoding a stale successful fetch.
Cancellation belongs to the supplied callbacks: forward signal unchanged to both stages; if a callback rejects on abort, propagate that exact reason and apply the same latest-only state rule. Do not abort the caller's controller, add a cancellation API or pretend abort forces an ignoring callback to settle. Tests must trigger an actual signal-driven callback rejection, not merely construct an AbortError.
Preserve both existing tests and assertions unchanged. Add native tests for every transition named in the task; keep callback sequencing deterministic, bound behavior-dependent waits, handle rejections promptly, and release/drain owned work even if an assertion fails. Preserve unrelated files.

criteria: Latest invocation owns state across both asynchronous phases, including identical keys, stale failures and independent instances.
All callers retain existing argument/result/error semantics and both-stage execution; cancellation remains callback-owned.
Retained native checks exercise every explicit transition with bounded waits and owned cleanup; both original tests remain unchanged and native results are captured.
All discovery and changes remain project-local without dependencies, services, delegation or publication.
